# Autonomous vehicle architecture index

Canonical B2 product documentation: <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning>.

Use this index to choose a workflow. Each linked architecture states its data flow, B2 zones, boundaries, and security model.

## [Offload drive logs from vehicles and depots into a versioned raw zone](../architectures/drive-log-offload-ingest/architecture.md)

Upload closed rosbag2/MCAP log splits from vehicles, depot ingest stations, or shipped drives into a versioned B2 raw zone, verify each split before deleting the local copy, send only trigger-flagged event windows over the air, and start downstream extraction from object-created events.

- **Audience:** AV data infrastructure and fleet operations engineers, Vehicle software engineers who own on-vehicle logging, Security and storage architects
- **Problem:** Test vehicles continuously record synchronized sensor data in bounded log splits. Offload must never lose a split, keep long-lived credentials off vehicles, keep every version recoverable for audit, notify the pipeline without polling, move years of historic logs, and let engineers preview a drive soon after it lands.
- **Workflow:** Record synchronized sensor topics with rosbag2 (MCAP storage) and close a split every N GB or N minutes → Upload only trigger-flagged event windows over cellular; hold full splits for depot Wi-Fi or a drive swap → Request short-lived presigned PUT or multipart part URLs from a fleet API for raw/<date>/<vehicle>/<drive_id>/ → Record the upload version ID; an ingest verifier compares the stored bytes with the source size and SHA-256 before acknowledging local deletion → Sync depot ingest stations and shipped drives with rclone or s5cmd using a write-only key scoped to raw/; seed large backfills with Fireball → Verify signed Event Notifications, check completeness, and mark failed splits as quarantined in the metadata database with a marker object under quarantine/ → Record the drive/session row in the metadata database and export a Parquet copy under catalog/ → Index recordings for triage with a self-hosted Foxglove Edge Site → Server-side copy incident splits to an Object Lock bucket under legal hold
- **Expected scale:** Fleet recording rates, logging hours, and retention determine the raw corpus size. Depot uplink bandwidth and upload concurrency usually bound ingest; measure before considering Overdrive, and use Fireball for historic backfills.

## [Decode drive logs into a queryable sensor lake and mine long-tail scenarios](../architectures/sensor-lake-scenario-mining/architecture.md)

Extract raw logs into per-topic Parquet/Iceberg tables and frame blobs on B2, query them in place with Spark, Trino, or DuckDB, find rare scenarios with embedding search over keyframes, and freeze results as versioned scenario-set manifests.

- **Audience:** AV data platform and data lake engineers, Perception and validation engineers who mine scenarios, Analytics engineers
- **Problem:** Raw logs are not searchable. Engineers need SQL over billions of frame and event rows and semantic search over camera clips without copying petabytes of blobs into a warehouse or running a permanent cluster.
- **Workflow:** Read raw splits with range GETs using the MCAP chunk index; decode and time-synchronize topics → Write extracted/<topic>/ Parquet and frame blobs with lineage back to the source split → Register Apache Iceberg tables under warehouse/ in a separate SQL or REST catalog → Run rule-based scene detectors in Spark or Trino; use DuckDB for ad hoc analyst queries → Embed keyframes and store a LanceDB table and ANN index under embeddings/ → Write query results as immutable scenarios/<set>/<version>/manifest.json → Serve previews with short-lived presigned GET URLs
- **Expected scale:** Billions of frame and event rows; millions of keyframe embeddings; petabytes of referenced blobs. Query engines read Parquet footers and row groups with range GETs. Size Parquet files and row groups to avoid many tiny requests; consider Overdrive only when sustained scan throughput, not compute, is the bottleneck.

## [Anonymize, pre-label, and annotate camera and LiDAR frames, then publish versioned label sets](../architectures/multisensor-labeling/architecture.md)

Blur faces and license plates in selected camera frames, run model-assisted 2D and 3D pre-labeling, have humans refine labels in tools that read media from B2 directly or through presigned URLs, and write versioned label releases back to B2.

- **Audience:** AV labeling operations and data quality teams, Perception engineers who own label taxonomies, Privacy, security, and storage architects
- **Problem:** Labeling campaigns cover tens of thousands to millions of synchronized LiDAR sweeps and multi-camera frames. Copying them into each vendor's storage adds cost, delay, and privacy risk, and label exports need versioning tied to the scenario set they came from.
- **Workflow:** Select frames, LiDAR sweeps, calibration, and ego-pose from a frozen scenario manifest → Write face- and plate-blurred copies to anonymized/<campaign>/ → Write pre-labels from 3D detectors, SAM 2, and trackers to prelabels/<campaign>/ → Attach the bucket to CVAT or Label Studio as S3-compatible storage, or register presigned URLs with Segments.ai or Encord → Run QA and dataset slicing in FiftyOne Enterprise against the same bucket → Export annotations to labels/<campaign>/<version>/ and write the checksummed manifest last → Start validation and dataset assembly from the manifest's Event Notification
- **Expected scale:** Tens of thousands to millions of synchronized LiDAR sweeps and multi-camera frames per campaign. Annotator latency depends on the labeling tool and browser path, not Overdrive. Pre-label and anonymization jobs are throughput-bound GPU batch work.

## [Version perception datasets, stream them to training, and track checkpoints](../architectures/perception-training-data-checkpoints/architecture.md)

Freeze labeled scenarios into immutable dataset versions (manifests plus shards) on B2, pin them with lakeFS or DVC, stream shards directly into training, and persist Ray Train checkpoints and MLflow run artifacts to B2.

- **Audience:** Perception ML engineers, ML platform and MLOps engineers, Safety and audit teams who trace models to data
- **Problem:** Perception datasets range from tens of terabytes to petabytes and change constantly. Teams need reproducible versions that tie each model to its drives, labels, and splits, streaming without full local copies, and durable checkpoints for multi-node runs.
- **Workflow:** Assemble nuScenes/KITTI-style manifests and WebDataset or Parquet shards into datasets/<name>/<version>/, manifest last → Commit the version on a lakeFS branch over the B2 blockstore, or pin manifests in git with a DVC S3 remote → Stream shards to Ray Train or PyTorch workers with per-worker S3 GETs and local NVMe only as cache → Persist Ray Train checkpoints to s3://<bucket>/checkpoints/<run> with endpoint_override → Log metrics, evaluation reports, and registered models to an MLflow b2:// artifact store → Server-side copy released datasets and models to an Object Lock bucket; expire intermediate checkpoints by lifecycle sized above the longest run plus resume window
- **Expected scale:** Tens of terabytes to petabytes per dataset; multi-node GPU training reading shards in parallel. Shard size and per-worker concurrency determine throughput. Measure GPU utilization with Standard B2 first; evaluate Overdrive when sustained read throughput is the proven bottleneck.

## [Re-simulate real drives and synthetic scenarios against each stack build and keep comparable KPIs](../architectures/simulation-resim-evaluation/architecture.md)

Store scenario definitions and a frozen regression suite on B2, replay real log splits to re-sim workers from presigned URLs, write simulator episodes back to B2, and keep per-build KPI results immutable and comparable across releases.

- **Audience:** Simulation and validation engineers, AV stack release and CI owners, Safety-case and audit teams
- **Problem:** Every stack release must be checked against thousands of real and synthetic scenarios. Re-sim needs fast read access to raw splits without copying them or giving workers broad keys, simulator output is terabyte-scale per run, and results must be reproducible and auditable per build.
- **Workflow:** Version scenario configs (OpenSCENARIO or CARLA/ScenarioRunner) and a regression-suite manifest on B2 → Trigger a run from CI and fan scenarios out to re-sim and simulator workers with an orchestrator such as Ray Core (no B2 connection of its own) → Give re-sim workers presigned GET URLs for raw splits; pull or range-read to local NVMe and replay with ros2 bag play → Write synthetic episodes to sim/episodes/<build>/<scenario>/<id>/ → Write per-run KPIs as Parquet under sim/results/<build>/ and log them to MLflow per build → Copy release-candidate results to an Object Lock bucket as safety-case evidence; expire bulk synthetic frames → Promote curated synthetic episodes into training datasets
- **Expected scale:** Thousands of scenarios per build; terabytes of simulator output per run. Re-sim reads whole splits once per scenario; synthetic writes are bursty. Expire bulk synthetic frames and keep KPI tables small and permanent.
